title: Traits
text:
We will measure the following functional traits.

LA: leaf area \(cm^{2}\)
LDMC: leaf dry matter content \(g.g^{-1}\)
LT: leaf thickness (\(\mu m\))
SLA: specific leaf area (\(g.cm^{-2}\))
TLP: leaf water potential at which leaf cells lose turgor (\(MPa\)), a key drought tolerance trait.
Nmass: leaf nitrogen mass content (\(mg.g^{-1}\))
Pmass: leaf phosphorus mass content (\(mg.g^{-1}\))
WD: wood density (\(g.cm^{-3}\),)

They will necessitate the following raw measurements:

Leaf fresh thickness (LT)
Leaf SPAD measurement (CC)
Leaf fresh weight (LDMC, SLA, RWC)
Leaf scan (LA, MajVLA)
Leaf saturated weight (RWC)
Leaf saturated water potential (TLP)
Wood dry mass (WDM)
Wood saturated volume (WSV)

title: TLP
text:
We extract the minimum osmometer measurement across the 10 measurement of one cycle per sample. We then compute \(\pi_0=\frac{-2.5}{100 \times osmo}\) using Van’t Hoff equation. Finally we computed TLP as \(\pi_{TLP} = 0.0832 \times \pi_0 - 0.631\) following Bartlett et al. (2012).


Code
lapply(1:5, function(i) 
  read_xlsx("data/raw/Belterra_2025/osmo/FEF25_TLP-12072025.xlsx", sheet = i)) %>% 
  bind_rows() %>% 
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(osmo = min(c_across(MES1:MES10), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select (1:3, osmo) %>% 
  mutate(pio = -2.5/1000 * osmo) %>%
  mutate(tlp = 0.832 * pio - 0.631) %>% 
  rename(vernacular = Especies, tree = Idtree, leaf = Idleaf) %>% 
  select(-osmo, -pio) %>% 
  write_tsv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/tlp_raw.tsv")




Code
read_tsv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/tlp_raw.tsv") %>% 
  group_by(vernacular) %>% 
  mutate(tlp_s = mean(tlp)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(vernacular = fct_reorder(vernacular, tlp_s)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular,
             tlp)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(aes(col = as.factor(tree)),
              width = 0.2, size = 3) + 
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Vernacular name", y = "TLP [ MPa ]") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none")













Bartlett, Megan K, Christine Scoffoni, Rico Ardy, et al. 2012. “Rapid Determination of Comparative Drought Tolerance Traits: Using an Osmometer to Predict Turgor Loss Point.” Methods in Ecology and Evolution 3 (5): 880–88.

Anomalies

anomaly: any anomaly in the generated masks:

ok: no problem
abn_area: abnormal area are masked, detected because they don’t have the shape of a leaf. Looking at the corresponding scan, it is because these areas correspond to some spaces between the folioles that are fully surrounded by leaf part. So they are interpreted as holes and filled.
fol_touch: this is the same problem than abn_area, except for the FAVA for which the foliolules are actually touching and form a compact area on the mask.
miss_petiolul: for double-compound leaves, the petiolule is not included, when it should have been
petiol_included: the petiole has been included, when it should not have
one_fol: just one foliole when the species has compound leaves

Damaged and young leaves
Raw leaf scans are manually checked for the following problems, but this is highly subjective:

ok: no problem (or very small area concerned)
damaged: part of the leaf or the whole leaf appears black/brown or yellowish on the scan or there are any other damages (except missing part of the leaf) suggesting that the leaf is decaying or is attacked by insects
young: the bright green colour of the leave compared to the other leaves from the individual and/or the species suggest non mature leaves

title: Junction
text:
Correcting typos in vernacular codes and tree ID
See the issues here and here to understand the rationale for these corrections.
Code
load_correct <- function(my_file, type ="tsv") {
  if (type == "tsv") {
    data <- read_tsv(my_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  }
  if (type == "csv") {
    data <- read_csv(my_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  }
  data <- data %>% mutate(
    vernacular = recode_values(vernacular,
                            "CUPUI" ~ "CUPIU",
                            default = vernacular),
    vernacular = recode_values(vernacular,
                            "PEQUI" ~ "PIQUI",
                            default = vernacular),
    tree = recode_values(tree,
                      8833 ~ 8883,
                      8383 ~ 8883,
                      6616 ~ 6617,
                      7734 ~ 7334,
                      default = tree),
    vernacular = if_else(tree %in% c(5685,6513), "FAVAO", vernacular)
  ) 
  if("comment" %in% colnames(data)) {
    data <-  data %>% select(-comment)
  }
  data
}

section: Checking for missing measurements in some datasets
text:
Checking for missing measurements in some datasets


Code
symdiff2 <- function(x, y, by) {
  x_sel <- select(x, all_of(by))
  y_sel <- select(y, all_of(by))
  diff <- union(setdiff(x_sel, y_sel), setdiff(y_sel, x_sel))
  if(nrow(diff) == 0) {
    print("There is a complete overlap between the two datasets")
  } else {
    print("The following tree/leaf are present in only one of the two datasets")
   diff %>% kable()
  }
}

title: Junction
section: Joining the datasets and calculating the trait values
text:
Joining the datasets and calculating the trait values
We join all the all raw measurements, botanical identification and the manual checks:


Code
traits_all <- plyr::join_all(
  list(tlp, hydrated, la, dry, check), 
  type = "full"
)


We add the botanical identifications made after the field campaign, using the inventory data of the 22/09/2026.


Code
inventory <- read_csv("data/raw/inventory/inventory_Belterra_20260922.csv",
                      locale = locale(encoding = "latin1")) %>% 
  select(PLACA, NOME_COMUM, NOME_CIENTIFICO, FAMILIA) %>% 
  rename(tree = PLACA,
         vernacular_full = NOME_COMUM,
         genus_sp = NOME_CIENTIFICO,
         family = FAMILIA)




Code
traits_all <- traits_all %>% 
  left_join(inventory)


We calculate the trait values.


Code
traits_all <- traits_all %>% 
  mutate(
    la = area_included,
    ldmc = dw/sw,
    sla = area_excluded/dw
  ) 


We create the file traits_all_raw.csv with all raw measurements, botanical identification and the manual checks, saved in derived data. No data have been corrected or excluded at this stage.


Code
traits_all %>% write_csv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/traits_all_raw.csv")

title: Junction
text:
Correcting for scan problems
The scans of the leaves that were touching the edge of the scanner have been manually corrected (see here and this issue).


Code
la_ex_1 <- read_csv("data/corrections/Belterra_2025/area_excluded_corrections.csv") %>% 
  select(Slice, `Total Area`) %>% 
  rename(slice = Slice, area_excluded_corr = `Total Area`) %>% 
  separate(slice, c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) %>% 
  mutate(area_excluded_corr = area_excluded_corr / (1275*1755) * (21*29.7))
la_in_1 <- read_csv("data/corrections/Belterra_2025/area_excluded_corrections.csv") %>% 
  select(Slice, `Total Area`) %>% 
  rename(slice = Slice, area_included_corr = `Total Area`) %>% 
  separate(slice, c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) %>% 
  mutate(area_included_corr = area_included_corr / (1275*1755) * (21*29.7))
la_ex_2 <- read_csv("data/corrections/Belterra_2025/area_excluded_corrections2.csv") %>% 
  select(Slice, `Total Area`) %>% 
  rename(slice = Slice, area_excluded_corr = `Total Area`) %>% 
  separate(slice, c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) %>% 
  mutate(area_excluded_corr = area_excluded_corr / (1275*1755) * (21*29.7))
la_in_2 <- read_csv("data/corrections/Belterra_2025/area_excluded_corrections2.csv") %>% 
  select(Slice, `Total Area`) %>% 
  rename(slice = Slice, area_included_corr = `Total Area`) %>% 
  separate(slice, c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) %>% 
  mutate(area_included_corr = area_included_corr / (1275*1755) * (21*29.7))
la_ex <- bind_rows(anti_join(la_ex_1, la_ex_2, by = join_by(vernacular, tree, leaf)),
          la_ex_2)
la_in <- bind_rows(anti_join(la_in_1, la_in_2, by = join_by(vernacular, tree, leaf)),
                   la_in_2)
corrections <- la_ex |> 
  left_join(la_in) |> 
  mutate(comments = "scan correction") |> 
  mutate(tree = as.numeric(tree), leaf = as.numeric(leaf)) |>
  mutate(vernacular = recode_values(vernacular,
                                    "PEQUI" ~ "PIQUI",
                                    default = vernacular))




Code
traits_cor <- read_csv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/traits_all_raw.csv") |> 
  left_join(corrections, by = c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) |> 
  mutate(
    area_excluded = coalesce(area_excluded_corr, area_excluded),
    area_included = coalesce(area_included_corr, area_included)
  ) |> 
  select(-area_excluded_corr, -area_included_corr)

title: Junction
text:
Correcting for duplicated leaves
We remove all instances of the two duplicated COPAI 6910 leaves (leaves 1 and 2), for all traits. For leaf 1 of COPAI 6896, we take the mean of the tlp values for the two measurements of this leaf and attribute it to leave 1.
See here).


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  filter(!(tree == 6910 & leaf %in% c(1, 2))) %>% 
  mutate(tlp = if_else(
    (tree == 6896 & leaf == 1),
    mean(tlp[tree == 6896 & leaf == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
    tlp)) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(comments = replace_when(
    comments,
    (tree == 6896 & leaf == 1 & comments !="") ~
      paste(comments, "tlp mean of 2 measurment", sep=" ; "),
    (tree == 6896 & leaf == 1 & comments =="") ~
      paste(comments, "tlp mean of 2 measurment", sep="")))


We recheck for duplicated leaves:


Code
dupl <- traits_cor %>% 
  group_by(vernacular, tree, leaf) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  filter(n>1)
if(nrow(dupl) == 0) {
  print("There are no duplicated leaves in the joined data.") 
} else { 
  print("The following leaves are duplicated in the joined data.")
  dupl %>% kable()
}


[1] "There are no duplicated leaves in the joined data."

section: Exploring and correcting the effects of leaf quality
text:
Exploring and correcting the effects of leaf quality

Incomplete leaves


Code
traits_long <- traits_cor %>% 
  gather(trait, value, la, ldmc, lt, tlp, sla) %>% 
  mutate(trait = recode(trait, 
                        "la" = "LA [ cm2 ]",
                        "ldmc" = "LDMC [ g / g ]",
                        "lt" = "LT [ µm ]",
                        "tlp" = "TLP [ MPa ]",
                        "sla" = "SLA [ cm2 / g ]"))


We first explore the effect of having an incomplete leaf, which affects la and indirectly sla.


Code
traits_long %>% 
  filter(trait %in% c("LA [ cm2 ]", "SLA [ cm2 / g ]")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular, value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(aes(col = as.factor(missing_part)),
              width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("0" = "black", 
               "1" = "orange2" ,
               "2" = "red2"),
    breaks = c("0", "1", "2"),
    name = "") + 
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ trait, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  xlab("") + ylab("")









Surprisingly, the incomplete leaves are not necessarily the smallest ones.
Let’s now check the distribution of these two traits if the leaves with a big missing part (i.e. missing_part = 2, see the scan page) are removed (in blue) compared to keeping the whole dataset.


Code
traits_long <- traits_cor %>% 
  gather(trait, value, la, ldmc, lt, tlp, sla) %>% 
  mutate(trait = recode(trait, 
                        "la" = "LA [ cm2 ]",
                        "ldmc" = "LDMC [ g / g ]",
                        "lt" = "LT [ µm ]",
                        "tlp" = "TLP [ MPa ]",
                        "sla" = "SLA [ cm2 / g ]"))
traits_long %>% 
  filter(trait %in% c("LA [ cm2 ]", "SLA [ cm2 / g ]")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  trait %in% c("LA [ cm2 ]", "SLA [ cm2 / g ]") &
                    missing_part !=2) ,
    aes(vernacular, value),
    color = "blue", fill = "blue", alpha = 0.1) + 
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ trait, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  xlab("") + ylab("")









Removing the very incomplete leaves has a big effect on the following species:

PIQUI: in some cases, 1 or 2 of the folioles were missing
PARAP: in some cases, several folioles were missing
COPAI: moderate change
CASTA: only two leaves removed, but they were missing a very big part

We remove the leaves with a big missing part (i.e. missing_part = 2, see the scan page) for LA and SLA. See this issue for the discussion.


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  filter(missing_part !=2)




Anomalies seen on the masks
As agreed in this issue and based on the scans examination (see scan page), we use unfilled area (area_excluded) even for LA, when anomaly is abn_area or fol_touch.


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  mutate(la = 
           if_else(anomaly %in% c("abn_area", "fol_touch"),
                   area_excluded,
                   la),
         comments = replace_when(
           comments,
           (anomaly %in% c("abn_area", "fol_touch") & comments !="") ~
              paste(comments, "unfilled area taken for la", sep=" ; "),
            (anomaly %in% c("abn_area", "fol_touch") & comments =="") ~
              paste(comments, "unfilled area taken for la", sep="")))         


Now, let’s look at the effect of other anomalies seen on the masks


Code
traits_long <- traits_cor %>% 
  gather(trait, value, la, ldmc, lt, tlp, sla) %>% 
  mutate(trait = recode(trait, 
                        "la" = "LA [ cm2 ]",
                        "ldmc" = "LDMC [ g / g ]",
                        "lt" = "LT [ µm ]",
                        "tlp" = "TLP [ MPa ]",
                        "sla" = "SLA [ cm2 / g ]"))

traits_long %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular, value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  anomaly =="ok"), 
    aes(vernacular, value), 
    width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  anomaly !="ok") ,
    aes(vernacular, value,
        col = as.factor(anomaly)) ,
    width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + 
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ trait, scales = "free_x", ncol = 5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  xlab("") + ylab("")









Although the cases of missing petiolule, petiole included or only one foliole considered doesn’t seem to affect the value, we remove them for LA, LDMC and SLA, as they are not following the protocol. Values for LT and tlp can be kept. See this issue.


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  mutate(la = 
           if_else(anomaly %in% c("miss_petiolul", "petiol_included", "one_fol"),
                   NA,
                   la),
         ldmc = 
           if_else(anomaly %in% c("miss_petiolul", "petiol_included", "one_fol"),
                   NA,
                   ldmc),
         sla = 
           if_else(anomaly %in% c("miss_petiolul", "petiol_included", "one_fol"),
                   NA,
                   sla))


Let’s check after excluding these values:


Code
traits_long <- traits_cor %>% 
  gather(trait, value, la, ldmc, lt, tlp, sla) %>% 
  mutate(trait = recode(trait, 
                        "la" = "LA [ cm2 ]",
                        "ldmc" = "LDMC [ g / g ]",
                        "lt" = "LT [ µm ]",
                        "tlp" = "TLP [ MPa ]",
                        "sla" = "SLA [ cm2 / g ]"))

traits_long %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular, value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  anomaly =="ok"), 
    aes(vernacular, value), 
    width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  anomaly !="ok" ) ,
    aes(vernacular, value,
        col = as.factor(anomaly)) ,
    width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + 
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ trait, scales = "free_x", ncol = 5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  xlab("") + ylab("")










NB: we will have to resample the PIQUI



Damaged and young leaves
Now, let’s look at the effect of anomalies seen on the raw scans:


Code
traits_long %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular, value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  raw_scan =="ok"), 
    aes(vernacular, value), 
    width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(traits_long,
                  raw_scan !="ok") ,
    aes(vernacular, value,
        col = as.factor(raw_scan)) ,
    width = 0.4, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + 
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ trait, scales = "free_x", ncol = 5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  xlab("") + ylab("")









The young leaves show clearly different values. According to our protocol stating that we sample on mature leaves, they should not have been included. We remove them.


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  filter(raw_scan !="young")


The effect of damaged leaves is much less clear (remember that here damaged refer doens’t refer to the fact that part of the leaf is missing, but rather to the quality of the leaf). We keep them and add a comment.


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  mutate(comments = replace_when(
           comments,
           (raw_scan == "damaged" & comments !="") ~
              paste(comments, "damaged leave", sep=" ; "),
            (raw_scan == "damaged" & comments =="") ~
              paste(comments, "damaged leave", sep="")))

Exploring and correcting outliers

                        "la" = "LA [ cm2 ]",

There is a big outlier for LDMC:


Code
out1 <- traits_cor %>% 
  filter(ldmc > 0.8) %>% 
  select(genus_sp, tree, leaf)
traits_all %>% 
  filter(tree == out1$tree & leaf == out1$leaf) %>%

  vernacular tree leaf      ldmc   sw     dw

The saturated and dry weight are very similar, there must be a typing error. We remove the ldmc value for this tree.

traits_cor <- traits_cor %>%

section: Save and explore the final trait data for the campaign
text:
Save and explore the final trait data for the campaign
The filtered and corrected trait dataset is save in the file trait_PlantForAdapt_Belterra_2025_vX.csv stored in output. See the README in output for the metadata.
Don’t forget to add a version name and update the NEWS. Update the metadata in Readme if needed.


Code
traits_cor <- traits_cor %>% 
  mutate(site = "Belterra",
         campaign = "2025") %>% 
  select(site, 
         tree, leaf, vernacular, vernacular_full, genus_sp, family,
         campaign,
         la, ldmc, lt, sla, tlp, comments) %>% 
  rename(verna_code = vernacular,
         vernacular = vernacular_full,
         botanical = genus_sp) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = str_squish(botanical), # remove multiple spaces if any
         genus = word(botanical, 1),
         species = word(botanical, 2)) %>% 
  relocate(site, tree, leaf, genus, species)




Code
write_csv(traits_cor, "outputs/trait_PlantForAdapt_Belterra_2025_vX.csv")


We look at the correspondence between the vernacular names we used during field collection and the botanical identification. The table below shows the vernacular names that correspond to more than one species:


Code
traits_cor %>% 
     group_by(verna_code) %>% 
  summarise(nb_sp = n_distinct(botanical)) %>% 
  filter(nb_sp >1)


# A tibble: 1 × 2
  verna_code nb_sp
  <chr>      <int>
1 CUPIU          2


Here are the two botanical names of CUPIU:


Code
traits_cor %>% 
  select(verna_code, vernacular, botanical) %>% 
  filter(verna_code =="CUPIU") %>% 
  distinct()


# A tibble: 2 × 3
  verna_code vernacular botanical                       
  <chr>      <chr>      <chr>                           
1 CUPIU      cupi£ba    Goupia glabra Aubl.             
2 CUPIU      lacre      Vismia cayennensis (Jacq.) Pers.




Code
traits_cor %>% 
  select(sla, tlp, , tree, leaf, genus, species) %>% 
  mutate(genus_sp = paste(genus, species, sep="_")) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  ggplot(aes(sla, tlp, col = as.character(tree))) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = genus_sp), method = "lm", 
              col = "grey", alpha = .2) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab(expression("SLA ["~cm^{2}~g^{-1}~"]")) +
  ylab(expression("TLP ["~MPa~"]")) +
  facet_wrap(~ genus_sp, scales = "free") +
  scale_color_discrete(guide = "none")









This figure is just made for exploration purposes, but we don’t expect the SLA-TLP relationship is not necessarly expected to hold intra-species. The higher LMA lower TLP relation holds good in inter-species relationships most of the time (it is often expected because high LMA is often linked to drought resistance strategies, and low TLP too, which is debatable). But this is not always the case (e.g. Isa’s work in Guyana).
